transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because of some things that happened at work. I work in HR, and... I pushed ahead with this big onboarding launch. I ended up committing company money and vendor time before any of the actual approvals were in place. 

At the time, it just felt bold, you know? Like it was absolutely necessary to just get it done and move things forward. But now... well, now I'm on leave, and everyone is asking me what I was thinking. So, that's why I'm here.
Can you describe how you were feeling in the days or weeks leading up to that decision at work? Were you feeling unusually energetic, confident, or excited?

Yeah, I definitely was. For the past few weeks leading up to it, I felt... well, brilliantly alive. Like I was finally going to show leadership what HR can really be. I had all this energy and confidence. 

But it wasn't just excitement. I also noticed I would get suddenly furious if anyone questioned me. Even over really small things, you know? Like if someone brought up minor edits to a document or just asked routine budget questions, I would just snap. So it was this mix of feeling completely unstoppable, but then getting incredibly angry if anyone pushed back or got in my way.
During that time when you were feeling so energetic and confident, did you find that you needed less sleep than usual?

No, I don't think so. Um... I mean, I had all that energy during the day, but I was still sleeping my normal hours at night. I didn't really notice any changes with my sleep, or feeling like I didn't need it. I was just getting my usual amount.

During that time when you felt so energized and confident, did you find yourself talking more quickly or urgently than usual, or felt a strong need to keep pushing forward with tasks without slowing down?

Yeah, I definitely did. Especially in meetings. I could actually hear myself talking a lot faster and... well, longer than I normally do. I'd just be jumping from topic to topic—like, I'd go from employee engagement to gallery layouts, and then right into retention metrics without really taking a breath. It was just a constant stream. People practically had to raise their hands just to get a word in or stop me.
Did you feel like you could function well or even prefer to go without sleep because your energy levels were so high?

No, like I said before, my sleep didn't really change. I was still sleeping my usual amount at night. I didn't feel like I could just skip sleeping or function without it, even with all that extra energy during the day.
During that time when you were feeling so energized and confident, did you ever feel like you didn’t need as much sleep as usual or could go longer than normal without sleeping?

I think we might be going in circles a bit here, but no. Like I mentioned just a minute ago, my sleep really didn't change at all. I never felt like I could just go without it or stay up all night. I was just getting my normal amount of sleep every night, even with all that energy.

During that time when you were feeling so energized and confident, did you feel that your abilities or importance were exaggerated, like you were destined for greatness or had special talents or powers that others didn't recognize?

No, I didn't feel anything like that. I mean, I felt good about my ideas at work and the things I was doing, but I didn't think I had superpowers or some special destiny. I just felt really confident in my normal abilities, nothing exaggerated or out of touch with reality like that.
During that time, even if you were still sleeping the same amount, did you feel like you could have gone with less sleep because you felt so energetic?

I really didn't. I know we keep coming back to the sleep thing, but... no. I never felt that way. 

Even with all that energy during the day, when nighttime rolled around, I needed my normal amount of rest. I was tired when it was time for bed. I never had that feeling where I thought I could just run on empty or get by on a couple of hours of sleep. It just wasn't a factor for me.
During that time when you were feeling so energized and confident, did you notice any changes in your appetite or feel like you didn’t need to eat as much as usual?
No, my appetite was pretty much normal. I didn't notice any changes there. I ate my usual meals and felt hungry at the normal times. So, no, nothing different with my eating habits.
During that time when you felt so energized and confident, did you feel like you didn’t need to eat as much as usual or could go longer than normal without eating?
No, like I just mentioned, my appetite didn't change. I didn't feel like I could skip meals or go longer without eating. I just ate normally, same as always.
During that time when you were feeling so energized and confident, did you notice that you weren’t as interested in food or that you could go longer than usual without feeling hungry?

Doctor, I feel like we're going in circles here. Like I said, no. Food just wasn't an issue. I ate my regular meals, I was hungry when I was supposed to be hungry. I didn't lose interest in food or go long stretches without eating. Everything with my appetite was completely normal.
During that time when you were feeling so energized and confident, did you notice any changes in your appetite — like not feeling as hungry as usual or skipping meals without it bothering you?

Look, I... I really don't know how else to say this. We've gone over this a few times now. My appetite was completely fine. I wasn't skipping meals, I didn't feel less hungry... eating was just normal. Nothing changed with my food.
Even if you were still going to bed at the same time, did you ever find yourself waking up much earlier than usual and feeling completely rested with less sleep than normal?
No, I didn't have anything like that. I've always been a pretty solid sleeper, so... no waking up super early or feeling rested after just a few hours. I just slept my normal amount.
Even if you were still going to bed at the same time, did you ever feel that you could get by with less sleep or that your usual amount of sleep was more than enough during that period?
No, like I just said, my sleep was completely normal. I didn't feel like I needed less sleep or anything like that. I just got my usual amount and felt fine.
Even if you were still going to bed at the same time, did you ever feel that you could get by with less sleep or that your usual amount of sleep was more than enough during that period?

I... I think you just asked me that exact same question. But no, like I just mentioned, I didn't feel like I could get by on less sleep. Everything with my sleep stayed exactly the same as it usually is.
Even if you were still going to bed at the same time, did you ever notice that you felt rested and ready to start the day much earlier than usual, even if you hadn’t slept as long as you normally do?

Doctor, I feel like we're going in circles here. You've asked me about waking up early and needing less sleep a few times now. The answer is still no. I didn't wake up earlier than usual, and I didn't feel rested on less sleep. My sleep just didn't change.
